provider_call_shape.error_envelope_rule: All errors MUST use ERR-1 envelope and INT_* subcodes.

rules: Adapters MUST be stateless with respect to business truth and MUST NOT cache provider secrets beyond the single provider call lifecycle.
Adapters MUST receive secret material only through SEC-1 authorized resolution and MUST NOT log it.
Adapters MUST classify errors as retryable, non_retryable, or circuit_breaker_signal using ERR-1 envelope fields.
Adapters MUST return provider_response_hash_sha256 instead of raw provider bodies unless the receiving domain explicitly owns encrypted raw payload retention.

ash_rules: All tenant-owned resources MUST use Ash 3.x multitenancy with explicit org_id context and Postgres RLS alignment.
ProviderWebhookReceipt MUST be append-only except for controlled state transitions represented as append-only receipt events or audited status transitions.
Route resolution MUST run in a service action that accepts tenant context explicitly and MUST NOT infer org_id from process dictionary or hidden defaults.

atlas.architect: INT-1 separates provider registry and routing from COMM/PAY/TKT business truth and from SEC-1 secrets.
atlas.assemble: Implementation MUST use Ash 3.x resources under Ticketing.Integrations and OTP app :ticketing.
atlas.link: INT-1 links COMM-1 dispatch to provider accounts, SEC-1 secret references, OBS-1 telemetry, OBQC-1 queue controls, and TEN-1 tenancy.
atlas.stress_test: INT-1 MUST fail closed on missing route, ambiguous route, disabled provider, missing secret_ref, signature failure, replay, tenant mismatch, and circuit-open states.
atlas.trace: Every provider resolution and webhook receipt MUST carry correlation_id, org_id or platform_org_id, provider_account_ref, provider_id, and deterministic idempotency_key.

changes: Renamed test-gates artifact to BP-0 Test_Gates filename format.
Raised ERR-1 dependency floor to v1.8.2 so INT_* subcodes are guaranteed registered.
Replaced fragile placeholder-ban wording with banned-token wording while preserving provider/secret boundaries.
change_log.summary: Provider-routing authority hygiene patch aligned to ERR-1 v1.8.2.

changes: Initial CS-0@3.0.0 INT-1 provider account, routing, adapter, and webhook governance contract.
Harden provider routing with explicit ProviderRoutingRule schema and deterministic resolver output.
Add ProviderSenderIdentity resource so communications sender/from/reply-to/domain posture is tenant-scoped without storing secrets in COMM.
Replace non-canonical webhook status quarantined with failed plus quarantine_reason/outcome fields.
Clarify inbound webhooks MUST NOT be circuit-blocked; circuit breakers affect processing and outbound provider calls.
Remove normative COMM-1 dependency from INT-1 to avoid reverse ownership/circular truth.
Add credential_mode rules so console/test providers can declare no secret while real providers require SEC-1 secret_ref.

change_log.summary: Final hardening: CS-compatible upper snake_case gate IDs, non-self-failing automated gate assertions, exact secret-field checks, and manifest regeneration for CS-0@3.0.0.

dependencies.reason: BP-0 defines the CS-0@3.0.0 blueprint discipline used by this bundle.
CS-0 defines the schema families and suite_schema target for this bundle.
TG-0 defines test-gate authoring conventions and deterministic assertion posture.
CG-0 defines strict CI expectations for bundle, manifest, dependency, and gate validation.
V42-0 supplies the constitutional tenancy, reliability, idempotency, and observability invariants.
TEN-1 governs org_id scoping, tenant context propagation, and cross-tenant denial.
IAM-1 governs actor identity, capabilities, step-up, and audited privileged operations.
ERR-1 governs canonical error envelope and stable INT_* subcodes registered for INT-1 v1.0.4 and later.
OBS-1 governs telemetry, alerts, runbooks, and SLO evidence.
OBQC-1 governs queue capacity, backpressure, and notification queue posture.
PSC-1 governs performance and safe-mode degradation requirements.
LOCKS-1 governs deterministic locking for publish, route resolution, and idempotent processing.

LINT-0 governs snake_case, banned-token rules, and repo-level anti-drift scanning.

deterministic_uuid_sorting.rule: When INT-1 hashes or signs lists of UUIDs, it MUST normalize each UUID to raw 16-byte form, sort by unsigned lexicographic byte order ascending, and MUST NOT sort UUID strings.

foundation_refs.reason: V42 requires org_id tenancy, idempotent side effects, Oban-only retries, and circuit-breaker posture for external dependencies.

fields.name: org_id
fields.notes: MUST be present for org-scoped accounts. MUST be null only when platform_scope=platform.

fields.name: secret_ref
fields.notes: Required when credential_mode=secret_ref. MUST be null when credential_mode=none.

invariants: ProviderAccount MUST NOT contain encrypted_credentials, api_key, password, private_key, token, refresh_token, smtp_password, or webhook_secret fields.
ProviderAccount.credential_mode=secret_ref MUST include secret_ref referencing SEC-1 and MUST be resolved only by authorized runtime adapters at final provider call time.
ProviderAccount.credential_mode=none MUST have secret_ref=null and MAY be used only for console/test providers or explicitly credentialless endpoints.
ProviderAccount with platform_scope=org MUST include org_id and MUST be protected by TEN-1 RLS.

ProviderAccount with platform_scope=platform MUST be readable only by platform-scoped capabilities and MUST NOT be selected for org traffic unless the routing rule explicitly declares platform_fallback_allowed=true.

resolution_contract: Routing resolution MUST accept an explicit selector object and MUST return exactly one active provider_account_ref or a typed INT error.
If zero active routes match, INT-1 MUST return INT_PROVIDER_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND and the caller MUST fail closed or defer according to its own safe-mode contract.
If more than one active route has the same highest priority for the selector, INT-1 MUST return INT_PROVIDER_ROUTE_AMBIGUOUS and MUST NOT choose nondeterministically.
Routing resolution MUST NOT read runtime.exs or application environment as the source of tenant provider truth.
Routing resolution MUST record provider_resolution_hash_sha256 over canonical_json(selector, matched_rule_id, provider_account_ref, route_version).

conditional_fields: purpose_id is required when a purpose-specific route is expected

invariants: ProviderSenderIdentity MUST NOT store provider credentials or DNS provider secrets.
Email sender identities MUST be verified before active routing can select them for production sends.
Org-scoped sender identities MUST NOT be usable by another org_id.
Platform-scoped sender identities MUST require platform capability and audit reason for change.

rules: Provider kind MUST be declared explicitly and MUST NOT be inferred from provider_id string values.
Provider capabilities MUST be declared before an account can be selected by a routing rule.
Provider capability declarations MUST be append-only; removing a capability from an active account MUST disable affected routes before deployment.

circuit_breaker_rules: Provider breaker state MUST be keyed by provider_account_ref and provider_operation.
Circuit-open state MUST prevent non-critical calls and MUST allow only domain-declared critical queueing behavior.
Provider 401/403 credential failures MUST disable affected ProviderAccount or route until reviewed; they MUST NOT be retried indefinitely.
reliability_and_safe_mode.inbound_webhook_rule: Inbound webhook receipt creation MUST remain available where technically possible and MUST NOT be circuit-blocked; processing MAY be deferred through Oban according to domain criticality.
reliability_and_safe_mode.retry_policy: All retryable provider calls and webhook processing MUST run through Oban; no inline retry loops are permitted.

boundary_rules: INT-1 MUST store only provider_account_ref, provider_id, provider_kind, route metadata, sender_identity_ref, and secret_ref pointers; INT-1 MUST NOT store api keys, smtp passwords, private keys, webhook signing secrets, oauth refresh tokens, or raw credentials.
INT-1 MUST NOT dispatch messages or mutate message state; calling domains MUST own their own dispatch, attempt, receipt, and business-state semantics.
INT-1 MUST NOT mark orders paid, issue tickets, post journals, or create refunds; domain-specific contracts MUST own those business truths.
INT-1 MUST provide deterministic route resolution for communications, payment, analytics, and webhook integrations without becoming the owner of those domains.

summary: Integration Provider Account, Routing, Adapter, Sender Identity, and Webhook Ingress Governance for CS-0@3.0.0.
title: INT-1 — Integration Provider Account, Routing, and Webhook Governance Contract

endpoint_rules: Webhook endpoint registration MUST be tied to provider_account_ref and webhook_secret_ref when the provider signs callbacks.
Inbound webhook controllers MUST verify signature before domain processing and MUST persist a receipt envelope quickly before async processing.
Signature failures MUST create a failed receipt with safe metadata and quarantine_reason=signature_invalid; they MUST NOT invoke domain handlers.
Inbound webhook receipts MUST be idempotent by provider_event_id when supplied, otherwise by sha256(canonical_provider_headers_subset + raw_body_hash + provider_account_ref).
Webhook replay detection MUST fail closed, MUST set failure_reason=replay_detected, and MUST emit INT_WEBHOOK_REPLAY_DETECTED.
Inbound webhook endpoints MUST NOT be blocked by outbound circuit breaker state; breaker state may defer processing but MUST NOT reject provider retries at ingress.
webhook_ingress.raw_payload_policy: Raw provider payload storage MUST be controlled by the domain-specific contract receiving the event. INT-1 MUST store raw_body_hash_sha256 and MAY store encrypted raw payload only when DATA-1 retention classification and SEC-1 encryption controls explicitly allow it.
